original_value: SummarySoftware‐defined networking (SDN) is a new network paradigm that is separating the data plane and the control plane of the network, making one or more centralized controllers to supervise the behaviour of the entire network. Different types of SDN controller software exist, and research dealing with the difficulties of consistently integrating these different controller types has mostly been declared future work. In this paper, the Domino framework is proposed, a pluggable SDN framework for managing heterogeneous SDN networks. In contrast to related work, the proposed framework allows research into SDN networks controlled by different types of SDN controllers attempting to standardize the northbound API of them. Domino implements a microservice plugin architecture where users can link different SDN networks to a processing algorithm. Such an algorithm allows for, eg, adapting the flows by building a pipeline using plugins that either invoke other SDN operations or generic data processing algorithms. The Domino framework is evaluated by implementing a proof‐of‐concept implementation, which is tested on the initial requirements. It achieves the modifiability and the interoperability with an average successful exchange ratio of 99.99%. The performance requirements are met for the frequently used commands with an average response time of 0.26 seconds, and the framework can handle at least 72 plugins simultaneously depending on the available amount of RAM. The proposed framework is evaluated by means of the implementation of a shortest path routing algorithm between heterogeneous SDN networks.

result.paraphrase: SummarySoftware-defined networking (SDN) is an emerging network paradigm that separates the data plane from the control plane, allowing one or more centralized controllers to oversee the behavior of the entire network. Various SDN controller software types exist, and research on the challenges of consistently integrating these different controller types has largely been left as future work. In this paper, the Domino framework is introduced as a pluggable SDN framework for managing heterogeneous SDN networks. Unlike related work, it enables research on SDN networks controlled by different types of SDN controllers while attempting to standardize their northbound API. Domino uses a microservice plugin architecture in which users can connect different SDN networks to a processing algorithm. Such an algorithm can, for example, adapt flows by constructing a pipeline with plugins that either invoke other SDN operations or generic data-processing algorithms. The framework is evaluated through a proof-of-concept implementation tested against the initial requirements. It meets the modifiability and interoperability requirements, with an average successful exchange ratio of 99.99%. Performance requirements are satisfied for frequently used commands, with an average response time of 0.26 seconds, and the framework can support at least 72 plugins simultaneously, depending on the available RAM. The proposed framework is assessed by implementing a shortest path routing algorithm between heterogeneous SDN networks.
